comparison.objective: Candidate commissions a shock absorber and retains its tuned setting; board-TK-HGKRZN evens conductor tips and twists on a wire connector until snug.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate uses hex-key insertion, counterholding, setscrew manipulation, fine collar rotation, and repeated impact observation. The splice requires translating one wire, grasping and rolling a connector clockwise through regrasping, and capturing both wire tips.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe dynamic stops, physical unlock-adjust-lock sequencing, and retained collar position. The splice requires the second wire captured within 3 mm, sufficient gripper-driven connector rotation, no exposed copper, snugness within 45 degrees, and release/home clearance.
comparison.reason: Fine rotation, alignment, and bimanual stabilization are shared primitives only. A threaded connector must capture and cover conductors; the candidate must tune energy absorption and mechanically retain a setting. Candidate numeric witness-torque/drift, rebound, overload, locking-torque, and thread-damage limits remain unspecified.
